answers.answer: For 2 players, deal 4 Player cards to each; for 3 players, 3 each; for 4 players, 2 each. Remove the Epidemic cards and set them aside before shuffling and dealing the remaining City and Event cards. Place each player's matching colored pawn in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 5–7: matching pawns in Atlanta; remove Epidemic cards; starting-card table.

answers.answer: Put the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2 space. Shuffle Infection cards; flip 3 and put 3 matching-color cubes on each named city, flip 3 more and put 2 on each, then flip 3 more and put 1 on each. Put all 9 revealed Infection cards face up in the Infection Discard Pile; the remaining cards form the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 8: leftmost ‘2’; groups of 3/2/1 cubes; 9 cards face up on discard, remainder form deck.

answers.answer: Use 4 Epidemics for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic; remove unused Epidemic cards from the game. Divide the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles, as equal in size as possible. Shuffle one Epidemic into each pile face down, then stack the piles into the Player Deck with smaller piles on the bottom.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7: difficulty counts and Player Deck preparation steps.

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions; you may repeat an action, paying its action cost again, or stop early. Action-cost cards go to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together, resolve any Epidemics first, and discard or play Events until within the 7-card limit; then Infect Cities by flipping cards equal to the current infection rate. After all three phases, play passes to the left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Actions: up to 4, repeats cost another action, action cards to Player Discard Pile.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry: move to a city connected by a white line; no card cost is listed. Direct Flight: discard the City card naming the destination to move there. Charter Flight: discard the City card matching your current city to move to any city. Shuttle Flight: from a city with a research station, move to any other city with a research station; no card cost is listed. White lines going off one board edge wrap to the other edge (the summary gives Sydney and Los Angeles as an example).
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table; Special Rules: Board wrapping.

answers.answer: Normally, spend an action, discard the City card matching your current city, take a research station from the supply, and place it in your current city. If all 6 stations are already built, relocate one from anywhere on the board. If the box supplied more than 6, set the extras aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Other Actions: Build a Research Station; Special Rules: Research station limit and extras.

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen cured color from the city, returning those cubes to the cube supply. It does not clear the other cured color or the uncured color in that same action: each different color takes a separate action. To clear the others, take additional Treat Disease actions, one color per action; for an uncured color, each action removes 1 cube, while for a cured color it removes all cubes of that color in the city. Removed cubes return to the supply.
answers.evidence: Treat Disease: 1 cube, or all cubes of one color if cured; each different color takes a separate action; return cubes to supply.

answers.answer: At any research station, spend an action and discard 5 City cards of the same disease color (4 if the player is the Scientist). The station city's color need not match the disease. Move that disease's cure marker to its Cure Indicator. Existing cubes remain, and the cured disease can still infect during normal infections and Epidemics until eradicated. If there are no cubes of that color anywhere on the board when the cure is discovered, immediately eradicate it and flip its marker.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure steps 1–3; ‘Existing cubes remain’; no cubes means immediately eradicate and flip.

answers.answer: The matching City card for the city both players occupy may be given to the other player or taken from that player. Both players must be in the same city, and both must agree. If the recipient reaches 8 cards, they must immediately discard a card or play an Event card to get within 7.
answers.evidence: Share Knowledge: give/take matching current-city card, same city, both agree; recipient over 7 immediately discards or plays Event.

answers.answer: The Researcher may give any City card from the Researcher's hand to a player in the same city, rather than only the matching city card. This transfer can happen on either player's turn. The exception only allows the Researcher to give a nonmatching card; it does not let another player give an arbitrary nonmatching City card to the Researcher.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Researcher exception specifies transfer from Researcher’s hand on either player’s turn and excludes arbitrary transfers to Researcher.

answers.answer: After the actions, draw 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 cards remain when you need to draw, the game ends and the players lose; the Player Discard Pile is not reshuffled.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards: top 2 together; fewer than 2 means loss; do not reshuffle discards.

answers.answer: Resolve the Epidemic in order: (1) increase the Infection Rate marker by 1 space; (2) draw the bottom Infection card. Since the named city has 2 cubes of that color, add only 1 cube to bring it to 3, then an outbreak occurs. Move the Outbreaks marker forward 1; place 1 cube of that color on each connected city, with chain-reaction outbreaks resolved after the current outbreak and no cube added to cities that already had an outbreak during this Infection card. If a connected city is already at 3 of that color, it outbreaks. Discard the drawn Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile. (3) Reshuffle only the Infection Discard Pile and place it on top of the Infection Deck. Remove the Epidemic card from the game; do not draw a replacement Player card for it.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: Increase, Infect (reach 3, then outbreak), Intensify; outbreak procedure; no replacement card.

answers.answer: The cards flipped per turn after 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 Epidemics are respectively 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, and 4.
answers.evidence: Infection Rate Track table, keyed by Epidemics Resolved.

answers.answer: Resolve all three steps of the first Epidemic, then all three steps of the second. An Event may be played between the two Epidemics. If the two drawn cards put a player over the hand limit, first resolve any Epidemics just drawn; only afterward discard cards or play Events until the hand is at most 7.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: two drawn at once resolve fully in sequence and Events may be played between; Hand Limit: Epidemics first.

answers.answer: During Infect Cities, flip cards from the top of the Infection Deck equal to the current infection rate, one at a time. For each card, normally place 1 matching-color cube in its named city. If that disease is eradicated, place no cube. If it is cured but not eradicated, the summary says it can still infect, so place the normal 1 cube (subject to the city's 3-cube limit); if the city already has 3, place no fourth cube and cause an outbreak. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities and Cure Procedure: top of deck at current rate; eradicated gets none; cured disease still infects until eradication; 4th cube causes outbreak; discard each card.

answers.answer: When the first outbreak resolves, move the Outbreaks marker forward 1 and place 1 cube of that color in every connected city. A connected city that already has 3 cubes of that color causes a chain-reaction outbreak after the current outbreak resolves; move the marker forward 1 again for that outbreak and spread its color to its connected cities. During chain reactions on this same Infection card, do not add cubes to cities that have already had an outbreak while resolving it, so the spread does not return a cube to the first city. Each city can hold multiple colors, up to 3 cubes of each color; the cap is per color, not shared across colors.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks: marker moves per outbreak; chain reactions resolve after current outbreak; skip cities already outbreaked this Infection card; up to 3 of each color.

answers.answer: No. Airlift cannot be played after the Infection card has been drawn but before resolving that card, because Events cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card. Once that card and its outbreak have resolved, Airlift may be played before the next Infection card is drawn. An Event is not an action; the player who plays it chooses its use, and the played card goes to the Player Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: any time, not an action; cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card; player decides use; discard to Player Discard Pile.

answers.answer: As an action, the Contingency Planner takes 1 Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and stores it on the Contingency Planner Role card; capacity is 1. The stored Event does not count against the hand limit. When played, remove it from the game instead of discarding it.
answers.evidence: Roles: Contingency Planner ability gives action cost, anywhere in discard, one-card limit, hand-limit treatment, and removal after play.

answers.answer: As an action, the Dispatcher may move any pawn to a city with another pawn, or move another player's pawn as if it were their own. The owner must agree when the Dispatcher moves another player's pawn. Direct/Charter Flight City cards are paid from the Dispatcher's hand; for a Charter Flight, the card matches the moved pawn's departure city, not the Dispatcher's location. When directing another pawn, the Dispatcher may move it but cannot make it Treat Disease or take other nonmovement actions. The Dispatcher cannot use the Operations Expert's special move.
answers.evidence: Dispatcher role entry lists both options, agreement, card payer and Charter origin, movement-only restriction, and Operations Expert exclusion.

answers.answer: Players win immediately when cures for all 4 diseases are discovered; diseases need not be eradicated and cubes may remain on the board. They lose if the Outbreaks marker reaches its last space (the 8th outbreak), if they cannot place the required number of cubes of a needed color because its supply is exhausted (during an Epidemic, outbreak, or infection; loss is immediate), or if a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after their actions because fewer than 2 remain. The Player Deck loss does not reshuffle discards.
answers.evidence: Victory; Defeat: three triggers; Cube supply check says immediate loss.

answers.answer: Put the board within reach and set the 6 research stations and disease cubes, separated by color, nearby. Place 1 research station in Atlanta; put the Outbreaks marker on 0 and the 4 Cure markers vial-side up near the Discovered Cure Indicators. Give each player a Reference card; shuffle Role cards and deal 1 face up to each, put matching colored pawns in Atlanta, and remove unused Role cards and pawns. The player with the highest-population City card goes first.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–5 and 9.

answers.answer: Teammates may offer advice, but the active player decides what to do. In Introductory play, keep cards face up for everyone to see. In Standard and Heroic, hands are private by default, though experienced groups may choose open hands. Anyone may inspect either discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: active player decides; Special Rules: Introductory face up, Standard/Heroic private by default with open-hand option, either discard pile inspectable.

answers.answer: Removing the last cube of an uncured disease does not eradicate it and has no effect. If the last cube of a cured disease is removed, that disease is eradicated and its cure marker is flipped to the eradication side. After eradication, no new cubes of that disease are placed during normal infections or Epidemics.
answers.evidence: Eradication: uncured last cube has no effect; cured last cube eradicates and flips marker; eradicated diseases get no new cubes.

answers.answer: The Epidemic's Infect step draws the bottom Infection card and places 3 matching-color cubes in the named city, unless eradicated. With zero cubes of that non-eradicated color there, place all 3. There is no outbreak merely because the city has reached 3; the summary says an outbreak occurs if the city already had cubes and the Epidemic adds only enough to reach 3. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile, then Intensify reshuffles only that pile and places it on top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: 3 cubes; if already cubes, add only enough to reach 3, then outbreak; discard card; Intensify.

answers.answer: Increase still occurs. During Infect, draw the bottom Infection card but place no cubes because its disease is eradicated; discard that Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile. Intensify still reshuffles only the Infection Discard Pile and puts it on top of the Infection Deck. The Epidemic card itself is removed from the game after resolution, with no replacement Player card.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards steps and note; eradicated diseases receive no cubes during infections or Epidemics.

answers.answer: The first Epidemic's Intensify empties the Infection Discard Pile. During the second Epidemic, its bottom Infection card is discarded into that pile; the second Intensify therefore shuffles only that one card and places it on top of the Infection Deck. The second Epidemic city, initially at zero cubes, receives 3 matching cubes. The next normal Infections draw that city first, and because it already has 3 matching cubes, that card causes an outbreak.
answers.evidence: Two Epidemics at once note: second bottom card is the only card shuffled, ends on top; city reaches 3 and is drawn first, causing outbreak absent prevention.

answers.answer: The Scientist needs 4 City cards of the same color instead of 5 to Discover a Cure. The player still must be at any research station, and the cards must still match the disease color; the station city's color does not need to match.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure and Scientist role: 4 for Scientist; at any research station and cards of disease color.

answers.answer: As an action, the Operations Expert builds a research station in the city they currently occupy. They need not hold, use, or discard a City card.
answers.evidence: Operations Expert role: as an action, build in current city with no City card needed, used, or discarded.

answers.answer: Once per turn, as an action, the Operations Expert may move from a city with a research station to any city by discarding any City card. The destination need not have a research station; the card need not match either city.
answers.evidence: Operations Expert role: once per turn as an action, move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card.

answers.answer: A Medic's Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen color from the Medic's city, even if that disease is uncured. It does not remove multiple colors with a single action; each color is a separate treatment choice/action.
answers.evidence: Medic role: Treat Disease removes all cubes of one color; Treat Disease instructions say each different color needs a separate action.

answers.answer: When the cure is discovered, if the Medic is already in a city with cubes of that cured color, remove all those cubes there immediately, without an action. Later, when another player moves the Medic into another such city by Dispatcher or Airlift on that player's turn, the Medic automatically removes all cubes of that cured color from the city upon entering, also without an action. Dispatcher/Airlift movement itself follows its own rules; the automatic cube removal has no action cost.
answers.evidence: Medic role: automatic removal in occupied city when cure discovered; entering via Dispatcher or Airlift on another player's turn also triggers it.

answers.answer: The Medic prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in the Medic's current city. This does not protect adjacent cities or uncured diseases.
answers.evidence: Medic role: prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in Medic’s city, not adjacent cities or uncured diseases.

answers.answer: The Quarantine Specialist prevents disease cube placement and outbreaks of every disease color in the Specialist's current city and all cities connected to it. This ability does not affect cubes placed during setup.
answers.evidence: Quarantine Specialist role entry.

answers.answer: Resilient Population removes any 1 card from the Infection Discard Pile from the game. It may be played between the Epidemic's Infect and Intensify steps, so it can remove the Infection card just discarded during that Epidemic before Intensify reshuffles the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Resilient Population removes any one Infection Discard Pile card from game; may be played between Infect and Intensify.

answers.answer: One Quiet Night skips the next Infect Cities step, so no Infection cards are flipped for that skipped step. It does not skip the Infect step of an Epidemic.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: skip next Infect Cities step (do not flip cards); does not skip Epidemic Infect.

answers.answer: Airlift moves any 1 pawn to any city. If it is another player's pawn, get that player's permission.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Airlift effect.

answers.answer: Only Player cards count toward the 7-card hand limit. Role cards, Reference cards, and the Contingency Planner's stored Event on the Role card do not count. To reduce a hand of 9 after drawing, first resolve any Epidemics just drawn; then discard cards or play Event cards until at most 7 remain.
answers.evidence: Hand Limit: Player cards only; Epidemics first, then discard or Events; Contingency Planner stored Event does not count.

answers.answer: Government Grant places a research station in any city, whether or not the player is there, with no City card discard needed.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Government Grant places a research station in any city (no card discard needed).

answers.answer: Forecast lets you draw, view, and rearrange the top 6 cards of the Infection Deck, then put those cards back on top of that deck.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Forecast effect.
